title: Drafting a cheque bounce notice without the mistakes that kill a case
p1:
A cheque bounce notice can look like a simple formality.

But one small mistake in drafting it can weaken the entire case before it even reaches the courtroom.
p2:
Many people believe that once a cheque is dishonoured, sending any legal notice is enough. That is not true.

The notice is not just a warning letter. It creates the foundation of the legal claim, and missing key details like the correct timeline, payment demand, or necessary facts can create avoidable problems.
p3:
A strong cheque bounce notice clearly connects the cheque, the reason for dishonour, the outstanding amount, and the legal requirement to make payment within the prescribed period.

The biggest takeaway: accuracy matters more than aggressive language. A well-drafted notice protects your position before the dispute escalates.
